To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
semantic and syntactic information both play a role in the production of noun phrase in Dutch.
the semantic and syntactic properties of the target nouns affected the speed and accuracy of the participants’ responses.

the production of a Dutch adjective noun phrase is faster when the target noun has the same gender as the target adjective than when it has a different gender, and that the production of an adjective noun phrase is slower when the target noun is from the same semantic category as the target adjective, compared to the production when it is from a different semantic category.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between lexical retrieval and sentence formulation.

how speakers select words that correspond with the meaning of the utterances they want to produce, and how the syntactic frame is constructed to accommodate the lexical representations that are retrieved.
the relationship between the retrieval of lexical information and the development of an appropriate syntactic frame.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the semantic and syntactic forces are both equally important in the production of noun phrase.

the results of the experiments are consistent with the idea that the retrieval of lexical items and the retrieval of syntactic information are not separate and independent processes but that they are interdependent.
the semantic and syntactic forces of a noun phrase production are both important.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
semantic and syntactic factors are involved in the production of Dutch noun phrases and that the semantic and syntactic representations of a noun are activated simultaneously.
the syntactic frame is built in part from semantic features.
the semantic and syntactic forces that guide the production of phrases are independent of each other.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the retrieval of a word’s gender can facilitate the production of a well-formed syntactic structure.
the retrieval of a lexical representation and the development of the frame for the sentence to be uttered is guided by the semantic and syntactic properties of the words to be used.
the retrieval of lexical information is guided by the syntactic frame that is being built in parallel.
